purpose: Preserve first-party explanatory source objects that may define Randolph's gas/refining mechanism before the July 13 indicator-selection claim without inflating the forecast count.

items.title: How Gas Prices Work
items.authorized_use: May inform source-defined mechanism only after directly inspectable transcript/caption content is preserved.

items.title: When Cheap Oil Doesn’t Mean Cheap Gas
items.authorized_use: The title supports only the descriptive possibility that cheap crude and cheap gasoline can diverge; it does not establish a forecast horizon or downstream target.

anti_inflation_rules: A descriptive or explanatory source is not a forecast merely because later events resemble its mechanism.
A forward-looking proposition may be promoted only from preserved first-party text or directly inspectable video/caption content.
Later July 13 indicator language does not retroactively convert June 25 or July 1 into forecasts.
Mechanism continuity across multiple Randolph objects may be represented as source lineage without duplicate forecast credit.
